about: Radio and intercom for chapter 9: leaving the Moon. Time lines hang on Apollo 17's jettison (GET 191:18:31) and transearth injection (GET 234:02:09); the jettison, the last loss of signal, the burn's start and end and the signal's return are cued by what happens (leaving-space.js works the times out). t = GET (seconds from liftoff). Original lines in the style of the Apollo air-to-ground; not quotes.

lines.text: America, Houston. You are go to jettison Challenger. She did everything we asked of her.
Ten seconds. Tunnel is vented, hatch is locked.
America, Houston. We will fly her down into the mountains by Taurus-Littrow for the seismometers. She has one more job to do.
America, Houston. Coming up on your last loss of signal. You are go for transearth injection. See you on the other side.
And there goes Houston. Just the three of us and the Moon.
Four minutes. Coming round to burn attitude. Nose first this time.
Ignition. Thrust is good. We are on our way home.
One minute. Look at that Moon go by.
America, Houston. How did it go?
Houston, America. The burn was on time. We are coming home.
Roger, America. That is the best news we have had all week.
There's the whole Moon in one window. We were down there.
